terms.grammar: adverb; as a noun with a genitive, “less of”: minus pecūniae
evidence: Ov. Rem. 94: crās minus aptus erit
Liv. praef. 12: quantō rērum minus, tantō minus cupiditātis erat
Cic. Div. 1.68: minus XXX diēbus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Before a number it often stands without quam, and the number keeps the case the sentence needs: minus XXX diēbus, in less than thirty days; paulō minus septingentī, a little under seven hundred, as subject. “The less …, the less …” is quantō minus …, tantō minus ….

evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.10.42–43: sī pede major erit, subvertet, sī minor, ūret
Sall. Jug. 49.2: nē pauciōrēs cum plūribus manum cōnsererent (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. back and forth: more or less

phrases.latin: quī nōn est hodiē, crās minus aptus erit
phrases.english: whoever is not ready today will be less so tomorrow

phrases.latin: adeō quantō rērum minus, tantō minus cupiditātis erat
phrases.english: so true is it that the less they had, the less they wanted

phrases.latin: Terentia minus bellē habuit, sed certum sciō jam convaluisse eam
phrases.english: Terentia has been less well, but I know for certain that she is better now

phrases.latin: Eō diē mīlitēs sunt paulō minus septingentī dēsīderātī.
phrases.english: That day a little under seven hundred soldiers were lost.

sources: Lewis & Short: parvus (minor, minus) · Lewis & Short: paucus · Lewis & Short: multus (plus)
